title: Chevalley intersection formula for Borel subgroups through a maximal torus
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All groups are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$, and all subgroup schemes are closed [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness is as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometrically connected means connected after extension to an algebraic closure $\bar k$. A torus is a group scheme $T$ with $T_{\bar k}\simeq(\mathbf G_m)^r$ for some integer $r\geq0$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. A Borel subgroup of $G$ is a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup, where solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. A maximal torus is a torus not strictly contained in another torus subgroup. Assume that $k$ is algebraically closed, $G$ is smooth and connected and $T\subseteq G$ is a maximal torus. Let $R_u(G)$ denote the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup of $G$, where unipotent means that all geometric points in a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation satisfy $(u-I)^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. Let $\mathcal B_T$ be the set of all Borel subgroups containing $T$. Put $I=\bigcap_{B\in\mathcal B_T}B$, the scheme-theoretic intersection (its ideal in the affine coordinate ring $k[G]$ is the sum of the ideals of these $B$). Denote by $(I_{\mathrm{red}})^\circ$ the reduced closed subscheme supported on the connected component containing the identity in $|I|$; reduction is as in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Then, as closed subgroup schemes of $G$, $$(I_{\mathrm{red}})^\circ=R_u(G)\cdot T,$$ where the right side is the scheme-theoretic image of multiplication $R_u(G)\times_kT\to G$, namely the closed subscheme defined by the kernel of its map on affine coordinate rings.

source.place: Theorem 17.56, first displayed equality, printed p.371; proof in section 17h, printed pp.373--375. Only the first equality is stated; its full generality in smooth connected affine groups is retained.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-general-borel-flag-variety], $\mathcal B_T$ is nonempty. Write $H=(I_{\mathrm{red}})^\circ$. The intersection is a subgroup scheme: on every test algebra it is the intersection of subgroups; equivalently its defining ideal is the sum of their Hopf ideals. It is affine of finite type since its coordinate ring is a quotient of $k[G]$. By [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component], $H$ is a smooth connected subgroup. The inclusion $T\to I$ factors through its reduction by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme], and through the identity component since $T$ is connected and contains the identity. Thus $T\subseteq H$. Choose $B_0\in\mathcal B_T$; then $H\subseteq B_0$, so $H$ is solvable: iterated commutators in $H$ map into the corresponding derived subgroups of $B_0$. The maximality of $T$ in $G$ implies its maximality in $H$.

source.place: Theorem 17.56, first equality; preliminary reduction to the solvable group I(T) in Section 17h, pp.373--375.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-solvable-unipotent-torus] to $H$ over the perfect field $k$. Obtain a smooth connected normal unipotent $U=H_u$ with torus quotient $q:H\to D=H/U$. By [lem-sfb-solvable-torus-complements], $q|_T:T\to D$ is an isomorphism. Let $s:D\to T\subseteq H$ be its inverse followed by inclusion. Multiplication $U\times_k T\to H$ has the inverse $h\mapsto(hs(q(h))^{-1},s(q(h)))$: the first coordinate lies in $\ker q=U$ and the two composites are identities on every test algebra. Consequently $H$ is exactly the scheme-theoretic image of $U\times_kT\to G$, since this map is the isomorphism just displayed followed by the closed inclusion of $H$.

source.place: Theorem 16.33(a)--(d), pp.335--336; the solvable decomposition implicit at the start of the proof of Theorem 17.56.

proof.text: Put $R=R_u(G)$ and $X=\mathcal B(G)$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-unipotent-solvable], $R$ is solvable. It is smooth and connected by its defining properties, so [lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point] applied to the nonempty proper $X$ supplies an $R$-fixed point $b_{B_1}$. The scheme-theoretic stabilizer equality of [lem-sfb-general-borel-flag-variety] gives $R\subseteq B_1$. For any Borel $B'$, transitivity supplies $g\in G(k)$ with $B'=gB_1g^{-1}$. Normality of $R$ gives $R=gRg^{-1}\subseteq B'$ as subgroup schemes. Hence $R\subseteq I$. Smoothness makes $R$ reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]; [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] and connectedness therefore give $R\subseteq H$. Since $U$ contains every smooth unipotent subgroup of $H$ by [lem-sfb-perfect-solvable-unipotent-torus], $R\subseteq U$.

source.place: The evident inclusion R_u(G) in every Borel; Theorems 17.9 and 17.3, pp.353--354, together with Theorem 16.33(b).

proof.text: For any $x\in X(k)$, take the reduced closure $Z=\overline{T\cdot x}$ of its $T$-orbit. By [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry] it is invariant, and by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] it is a nonempty proper finite-type scheme, as a closed subscheme of $X$. Apply [lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point] to the torus $T$ acting on $Z$; tori are commutative and hence solvable. It gives a $T$-fixed $b_B\in Z(k)$, with $B\supseteq T$ by [lem-sfb-general-borel-flag-variety]. Thus $x\in A_B$ by the rational-point description in [lem-sfb-luna-borel-attraction-charts]. We have proved that every rational flag belongs to such a chart. The node on charts applies with $V=U$, because $U\subseteq H\subseteq B'$ for every $B'\supseteq T$. Each $A_B$ is affine and $U$-invariant.

source.place: Section 17h, p.375, paragraph proving that the opens B(B) cover the flag variety; Theorem 17.65, p.374.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X(k)$ and let $O=U\cdot x$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry] its reduced closure $Z_U$ is $U$-invariant. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. The smooth connected unipotent $U$ is solvable by [lem-sfb-smooth-unipotent-solvable]; hence [lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point] gives a $U$-fixed point $y\in Z_U(k)$. Choose $A_B$ containing $y$, as in the preceding step. Its closed complement is $U(k)$-invariant by [lem-sfb-luna-borel-attraction-charts]. If any rational point of $O$ lay in that complement, transitivity of $U(k)$ on $O(k)$ would put all of $O(k)$ there. This implies $O$ lies there as a subscheme: the inverse image of the open $A_B$ in the orbit morphism from the affine reduced $U$ would otherwise be a nonempty open with a $k$-point, by [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing]. The closed complement would then contain $Z_U$ and $y$, a contradiction. Thus $O\subseteq A_B$.

source.place: Section 17h, last paragraph, p.375, through the containment of the orbit in B(B).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-kostant-rosenlicht-affine-orbits] to $U$ acting on the affine finite-type scheme $A_B$: $O$ is closed in $A_B$. Since $y\in\overline O\cap A_B$ and $O\subseteq A_B$, it follows that $y\in O$. A $U$-fixed rational point in a transitive orbit forces that orbit to be a singleton: if $y=u_0x$, then $x=u_0^{-1}y=y$, and every $ux=y$. Thus every $u\in U(k)$ fixes every $x\in X(k)$. For $x=b_{B'}$, the scheme-theoretic stabilizer of [lem-sfb-general-borel-flag-variety] gives $U(k)\subseteq B'(k)$. The affine $U$ is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Every equation of $B'$ restricts to a function on $U$ vanishing on all $U(k)$; it is zero by [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing]. Therefore $U\subseteq B'$ as subgroup schemes for every Borel $B'$, including those not containing $T$.

source.place: Section 17h, last paragraph, p.375, from Kostant--Rosenlicht to triviality of the orbit; scheme-theoretic upgrade using reducedness and the affine vanishing principle.

proof.text: Let $J$ be the scheme-theoretic intersection of all Borel subgroups, and put $K=(J_{\mathrm{red}})^\circ$. As for $I$, the sum of the defining Hopf ideals represents $J$ as an affine finite-type subgroup. By [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component], $K$ is smooth and connected. Since $K\subseteq B_0$, commutator termination in $B_0$ proves that $K$ is solvable. Conjugation by each $g\in G(k)$ permutes the Borels and preserves their intersection, its reduction and its identity component, as closed subgroup schemes. Hence $K$ is normal in $G$ by [lem-sfb-smooth-ambient-normality-geometric]. The preceding step gives $U\subseteq J$; reducedness and connectedness give $U\subseteq K$, using [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] and [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme]. Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-solvable-unipotent-torus] to $K$: its smooth connected unipotent subgroup $K_u$ contains $U$, and is normal in the smooth ambient $G$. By the defining maximal property of $R_u(G)$, $U\subseteq K_u\subseteq R_u(G)$.

source.place: Section 17h, pp.374--375, reduction to Remark 17.31, p.361; Theorem 16.33 and Proposition 1.90. The reduced full intersection itself supplies the normal solvable subgroup needed here.

proof.text: The two inclusions give $U=R_u(G)$ as closed subgroup schemes. Substituting into the scheme-theoretic image identity from step 2 yields $$(I_{\mathrm{red}})^\circ=H=R_u(G)\cdot T.$$ In particular the conclusion is an equality of the specified closed subgroup schemes, with the product defined by the kernel on coordinate rings, and not just an equality of rational-point sets.

source.place: Theorem 17.56, first displayed equality, p.371; conclusion of Section 17h.

proof_origin.place: Section 17h, Theorems 17.64--17.65 and proof of Theorem 17.56, printed pp.373--375; Theorem 16.33 and Remark 17.31 made explicit.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q03-76b236725 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Milne iAG2017 17.56 (p.371), §17h with 17.64, 17.65 and the proof of 17.56 (pp.373-375), 17.9, 17.48, and §17f with 17.52. The item statement is verbatim (identical to live and side-live, item still unsplit live), with no weakening. The 8 steps follow Luna's proof in Milne. Step 1: identity component plus reduced factorization gives H smooth, connected and solvable, with T maximal in it. Step 2: perfect-solvable H_u plus torus complements, with the explicit inverse checked, gives H = U·T as the scheme image. Step 3: fixed point plus scheme stabilizer plus conjugacy plus normality gives R_u ⊆ U. Steps 4-6: T-orbit closures put every rational point in a chart; the invariant complement of a chart puts each U-orbit in it; Kostant-Rosenlicht in the affine chart makes each orbit trivial; the vanishing principle gives U ⊆ every Borel scheme-theoretically. Step 7: the full intersection K is normal by smooth-ambient-normality-geometric, so U ⊆ K_u ⊆ R_u(G). All hypotheses were checked against the cited statements; def-sfb-solvable-group-structure reconciles the solvability conventions. New nodes: the general flag variety (true, X = G/B; stabilizer, conjugacy and fixed-point clauses checked; reductive-pair, solvable-flag and Picard nodes are not duplicates); the Luna charts (a faithful generalization of 17.65, since the proof uses only V ⊆ the parabolic stabilizer; checked via the B^- big cell; not the item restated); Kostant-Rosenlicht (17.64, connected case). No duplicates in snapshot or live (rg Borel, Rosenlicht, attraction). No cycle: the closure has neither the item nor its citer.
